requirements.title: Host association gives inner scoping units access to host entities with preserved identity and attributes
requirements.definition: Derived-type definitions, interface bodies, internal subprograms, module subprograms, and submodules access host entities as specified by IMPORT and host rules. Host-associated variables are previously declared, other host-associated entities are previously defined, internal subprograms access their host instance, and accessed entities use the same identifier and attributes except for separately registered ASYNCHRONOUS and VOLATILE permissions.

pending.derived-type-host-access: Host integer kind parameter k=selected_int_kind(2) and type component uses integer(k); constructing the type stores exact 42 and exposes loss of host access.
pending.interface-body-host-access: Interface body with IMPORT of host type box declares a dummy of type box; source-control uses component value 42 in the eventual procedure contract and leaves IMPORT syntax to 8.8.
pending.internal-subprogram-host-instance-access: Host integer x=1; internal procedure without local declaration sets x=2; after the call host x is exactly 2, contrasting the local-declaration companion in p2.
pending.module-subprogram-host-access: Module procedure body reads module integer x initialized to 42 into observed=-777; exact observed=42 proves host access for the module subprogram.
pending.submodule-host-access: Submodule procedure reads ancestor module integer x=42 into observed=-777; exact observed=42 proves host access without adding a duplicate submodule fixture here.
pending.host-variable-previously-declared: Internal procedure assigns host integer x before any local declaration; x starts 1 and exact post-call x=42 confirms the host declaration is usable.
pending.host-nonvariable-previously-defined: Internal procedure constructs host type box(42) and calls host generic g(1) returning 77; exact sentinels expose missing type or generic host definition.
pending.host-identifier-and-attributes-preserved: Host parameter p=42 and target integer t=5 are used inside an internal procedure for an array bound and pointer association; exact p-derived extent 1 and ASSOCIATED(q,t) true check attributes.
pending.host-accessed-entity-kinds: Source-control inventory covers named data objects, nonintrinsic types, abstract interfaces, procedures, generic identifiers, and namelist groups with one exact sentinel plan per kind in owning catalogues.

requirements.title: Host-associated locals may add ASYNCHRONOUS and VOLATILE attributes in local scope
requirements.definition: A local entity may have ASYNCHRONOUS even though the host entity does not, and a noncoarray local entity may have VOLATILE even though the host entity does not.

pending.host-associated-volatile-local-permitted: Host noncoarray integer x=42 lacks VOLATILE; internal procedure declares VOLATILE :: x, copies x to observed=-777, and expects exact 42 without optimization-dependent assertions.

requirements.title: Use association and global identifiers make same-named host entities inaccessible by that nongeneric name
requirements.definition: A use-associated entity with the same nongeneric name as a host entity makes the host entity inaccessible by that name. An external procedure name given EXTERNAL or a name used as a module-name in a USE statement is a global identifier and makes any host entity with that nongeneric name inaccessible by that name.

pending.use-associated-name-hides-host: Host integer x=101; internal procedure USEs module provider, ONLY: x where provider x=202, assigns observed=x, and after return observes observed=202 and host x=101. Wrong host resolution would give observed=101 or would change host x rather than reading provider x. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.external-global-name-hides-host: Host integer x=103; internal procedure declares integer external function x returning 204 and calls x(); observed=204 and host integer x remains 103. Wrong host resolution would try to use the host integer as a procedure or yield 103 rather than the external result 204. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.module-name-global-hides-host: Host integer m=105; internal procedure contains USE m for a module m exporting value=206 and records value=206 by the imported name while host integer m remains 105. Wrong host resolution would use or change host m=105 rather than the module entity value 206. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.

requirements.title: The listed local identifiers make same-named host entities inaccessible by host association
requirements.definition: Each listed occurrence that makes a name local in the scoping unit makes any host entity with that nongeneric name inaccessible by that name: function-name, object-name declarations and attribute statements, type-param-name, named constant, coarray-name, array-name, common-block variable-name, EXTERNAL procedure pointer, DATA-initialized variable, EQUIVALENCE object, dummy argument, result name, interface-body entity, intrinsic procedure name, namelist group name, enum type name, enumeration type name, generic name, named construct, plus a derived type name or procedure name defined by an applicable host scoping unit.

pending.local-function-name-hides-host: Host integer x=107; an internal procedure contains local integer function x() returning 208 and assigns y=x(); after the call host x remains 107 and y=208. Wrong host resolution would not call the local function and would yield host value 107 or an invalid integer-as-function use. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-object-declaration-hides-host: Exact sentinel requested by the packet: host integer x=1; internal procedure declares integer x, sets local x=2, and returns; host x remains 1. Wrong host resolution would change host x to 2. This is also the shared positive control for the p2 local-identifier plans: without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-type-param-name-hides-host: Host integer n=109; internal procedure declares a derived type with local type parameter n=210 and constructs an object whose LEN or KIND-derived value records 210 while host n remains 109. Wrong host resolution would use host n=109 for the parameter-derived value. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-named-constant-hides-host: Host integer x=111; internal procedure declares integer, parameter :: x=212 and assigns observed=x; exact observed=212 and host x=111 expose local PARAMETER resolution. Wrong host resolution would read 111. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-coarray-name-hides-host: Source-control sentinel records host integer x=113 and inner coarray declaration integer :: x[*] with a planned local value 214; coarray execution remains out of scope, but wrong host resolution would address or change host x=113 rather than the local coarray name. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-array-name-hides-host: Host scalar integer x=115; internal procedure declares local integer, dimension(1) :: x, sets x(1)=216, and host scalar x remains 115 after the call. Wrong host resolution would change or read the scalar host x=115 rather than local element value 216. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-common-variable-hides-host: Host integer x=117; internal procedure declares integer x; common /blk/ x; assigns common x=218; host x remains 117 and a separate common reader observes 218. Wrong host resolution would change host x to 218 and leave the COMMON sentinel unchanged. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-procedure-pointer-external-hides-h: Host procedure pointer x is associated with host_target returning 119; internal procedure declares procedure(integer), pointer :: x with EXTERNAL path and associates it to local_target returning 220; local call returns 220 and the host pointer still returns 119 after the call. Wrong host resolution would call the host pointer and return 119. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-data-initialized-variable-hides-ho: Host integer x=121; internal procedure has local integer x; DATA x /222/; the first reference after DATA returns observed=222 while host x remains 121. Wrong host resolution would read host x=121 or change host x, and the p3 restriction separately keeps reference/definition after DATA. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-equivalenced-object-hides-host: Host integer x=123; internal procedure declares local integers x,y; equivalence (x,y); sets y=224 and observes local x=224 through equivalence while host x remains 123. Wrong host resolution would change host x or fail to show the local equivalence sentinel 224. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-dummy-arg-name-hides-host: Host integer x=125 and actual a=226; internal subroutine inner(x) assigns dummy x=227; calling inner(a) leaves host x=125 and sets a=227. Wrong host resolution would change host x to 227 and leave actual a=226. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-result-name-hides-host: Host integer x=127; internal function f() result(x) sets result x=228; calling f gives 228 and host x remains 127. Wrong host resolution would change host x or return 127 rather than result value 228. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.

Wrong host resolution would use the host integer value 129 or reject integer-as-procedure instead of the interface procedure result 230. pending.local-intrinsic-procedure-name-hides-hos: Host external integer function abs returns 42+n, so abs(-3) would be 39 through host association; internal procedure declares intrinsic abs and observed=abs(-3) gives exact 3. Wrong host resolution would produce 39, not 3. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.

Wrong host resolution would use host integer x=135 rather than enumeration-type sentinel 236. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-generic-name-hides-host: Host generic x resolves an integer specific returning 137; internal interface x maps to local specific returning 238; observed call x(0) gives 238 and the host generic still returns 137 outside. Wrong host resolution would return 137. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-named-construct-hides-host: Host integer x=139; internal procedure uses named block x: block and records observed=240 inside the construct, with host x remaining 139. Wrong host resolution would use host value 139 or change host x rather than the named-construct control path value 240. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-derived-type-name-hides-host: Outer host integer x=141; an inner derived-type definition named x has a component default sentinel 242 and constructing that local type records 242 while host integer x remains 141. Wrong host resolution would use host integer 141 or make the local type construction unavailable. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.
pending.local-procedure-name-hides-host: Outer host integer x=143; an internal procedure named x returns 244 and is a local identifier of its host scoping unit, while the outer host integer x remains 143. Wrong host resolution would use host value 143 or reject the procedure call instead of returning 244. Shared positive control: local-object-declaration-hides-host demonstrates the companion; without a local identifier, the inner scope changes host x.

requirements.title: Implicit-interface external or dummy procedures accessed by host association need host EXTERNAL and host-established function type
requirements.definition: An external or dummy procedure with an implicit interface accessed via host association shall have the EXTERNAL attribute in the host scoping unit; a function invocation in the inner scoping unit also requires its type and type parameters to be established in the host scoping unit. Function type and type parameters are established by explicit declaration, invocation, module access, or host access from a scope where established.

pending.host-function-type-establishment-paths: Source-control matrix records four conforming host establishments: explicit integer declaration, a host invocation assigning exact 45, module access to an integer external, and host access from an ancestor scope that already established integer type.
